About the texts and English

All 441 biblical verses in Isaiah 1–23 are included. The five classical commentators are reproduced in full Hebrew wherever the source supplies a comment. Every biblical verse appears in every view. Where no separate commentary is supplied, the biblical verse stands on its own. References to comments on other verses remain in their original positions. Each reading begins with an original bilingual chapter overview. Abarbanel alone is arranged as the complete biblical chapter followed by his complete commentary; the other views retain their verse-by-verse layout.

The English Bible is the public-domain Jewish Publication Society translation of 1917, accessed through Sefaria. English commentary translations were prepared for this reader from the displayed Hebrew, paragraph by paragraph. They include the quotations, references, grammatical discussions, and alternative interpretations. Bracketed translator notes identify genuinely unclear source wording or necessary clarification.

The published English Rashi by Rabbi A. J. Rosenberg, Judaica Press Complete Tanach with Rashi, supplied by ALHATORAH under CC BY 3.0, was consulted or adapted where applicable. The displayed Hebrew controls the content and order of each translation, including additions that differ from that published version.

Torat HaGeonim contains the excerpts you originally supplied, at 4:4, 5:1, 6:1–3, and 6:6–7, with full English translations. It is not a complete Geonic collection for chapters 1–23.

Ralbag’s Isaiah commentary is not extant, so this reader does not contain attributed Ralbag commentary or lessons on these chapters. See History of Jewish Philosophy, discussion of Gersonides.

Hebrew sources: ALHATORAH.ORG, Mikraot Gedolot. Modern editorial apparatus is generally omitted. Jewish chapter numbering is used throughout: Isaiah 8:23 corresponds to 9:1 in many English Bibles. Font: Noto Serif Hebrew, SIL Open Font License 1.1.
